title: Fallback rule engine for pinned models with priority scoring
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement:
Teams pin model versions to ensure deterministic outputs for production workflows. When a pinned version becomes unavailable (capacity, regional outage, or deprecated), current behavior is either blanket failure or coarse fallback to the default model variant. This causes availability gaps, silent quality regressions, and unpredictable cost/latency trade-offs for customers using pinned versions.

Goal:
Build a flexible, auditable fallback rule engine for pinned model versions that: (1) enumerates fallback candidates (region, identical arch variants, quantized variants, newer minor versions), (2) scores candidates with a priority/weighting function that accounts for compatibility, performance profile, cost, and deprecation status, (3) exposes operator controls and rollout knobs in the Console and API, and (4) emits telemetry and audit logs for every fallback decision.

Non-goals:
- Automatic model retraining or automated quality evaluation of fallback outputs (outside scope).
- Replacing global routing/policy layer; this is a decision layer invoked when a pin cannot be satisfied.

Design summary:
1) Rule engine core: express a fallback plan as an ordered set of rules with optional scoring weights. Rules can reference region, model-variant tags (e.g., quantized, fp16), pinned-version compatibility ranges (semver-ish), and deprecation flags. The engine returns a ranked list of candidate endpoints.

2) Scoring function: base score starts from compatibility (exact version match score=100), reduced by delta for variant (e.g., quantization -10, lower compute tier -20), latency penalty from perf profile (+/− based on 95p), and deprecation penalty (configurable per-customer; default -50 for deprecated major versions). The final score also factors cost multiplier and availability (binary: reachable/unreachable).

3) Policy evaluation and operator controls: Console UI to preview fallback chains for a pinned version. API to submit per-organization fallback policy overrides (allow/deny quantized fallbacks, max allowed latency increase, allow cross-region failover). Canary rollout mechanism: start with dry-run logging, then opt-in enforcement.

4) Deprecation handling: When a model is marked deprecated, pins remain functional but get a deprecation score penalty. For scheduled deprecations we will surface affected organizations in Console and trigger email notifications. A forced-block deprecation (security) path can be used by platform ops to bail out of any fallback and return structured error to callers.

5) Telemetry & observability: Each fallback decision emits: pin_key, request_id, attempted_version, chosen_candidate, reason_code, score_breakdown, region, latency_estimate, and whether fallback was dry-run. Dashboards and alerts for unexpected increases in fallback rate or when fallback choices cross cost/latency thresholds.

API changes (proposal):
- New field in inference request: "pin_policy_context" (optional) where customer can supply enforcement mode: dry_run | enforce | enforce_with_approval.
- Admin API: GET/PUT /orgs/:id/pin-fallback-policy to view/update org-level defaults.

Acceptance criteria:
- Engine returns deterministic candidate ranking for 95% of pinned mismatch cases for our model catalog.
- Dry-run mode available and logs every decision without altering routing.
- Console shows fallback chain preview for a pinned version and a CTA to simulate request-level behavior.
- Metric: fallback_rate per org/day instrumented; alert if >2% unexpectedly for a major release change.
- Integration tests cover cross-region, quantized variant, and deprecated-version paths.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Implement engine core and scoring, unit tests, and instrumentation (dry-run only).
- Week 2: Expose API + Console preview in alpha, internal-only customers opt-in.
- Week 3: Expand to broader customers, enable enforcement opt-in.
- Week 4: Default enforcement for new pins, migration tooling for existing pins and a final deprecation notification flow.

Trade-offs considered:
- Simpler approach (static ordered lists) vs scoring: we chose scoring for finer-grained trade-offs but it adds complexity in transparency and debugging. To mitigate, we will provide detailed score breakdowns.
- Cost: allowing quantized or lower-tier variants reduces unit cost but can introduce subtle quality drift. Make it opt-in per org by default for high-importance customers.
- Consistency vs availability: prefer availability with an opt-in strict mode for customers who require bit-for-bit reproduction.

Migration notes:
- Existing pins with no explicit fallback policy inherit org default: allow_same_variant_only. We will run a migration job that flags pins affected by scheduled deprecations and create a support/batched email to owners.

Security/review: no immediate secrets exposure, but audit logging and RBAC must be validated. Security review required before enforcement for private deployments.
